name: glm53-sparse-v1
purpose: Sparse-frontier qualification: 2093 IDs (sparse_qualification_text in crates/qwen-llm/src/glm5_next_metal/tests.rs: the qual-v1 passages plus twelve more) through llama.cpp serial decode, plus a capture run of the indexer inputs and outputs at positions 2050-2060 (visible lengths 2051-2061: the dense-equivalent control, the first exclusion at 2052, every tail length).
token_source: tokens.txt in the location below; tests re-tokenize the text and assert every oracle record's token matches

producer.device: Apple M4 Max 128 GB, Metal, all layers offloaded

serial.bin.run: logits only, n_batch = n_ubatch = 1, all 2093 positions

observations: The capture run's logits are byte-identical to the logits-only run at all 2093 positions: these captures do not perturb llama.cpp.

Shapes: indexer_q [128, 32] F32 (rounded to F16 inside the fused lightning indexer), indexer_weights [32] (already scaled by 1/64), indexer_pool_k [128, 576] (padded past the visible pools), indexer_score [576] (-inf past visibility), indexer_top_k I32 [512] ordered by descending score.

Component replay: the native 32-head half-matrix scorer on these inputs reproduces indexer_score bitwise (relative error 0) at all 121 (position, block) cases; native selection equals llama.cpp's set at all 110 sparse cases; at position 2050 llama.cpp selects every visible pool.

End to end: Exact packed prefill of 2048 tokens then teacher-forced native decode of positions 2048-2092 agrees with serial.bin on top-1 at all 46 positions with zero choice regret; worst KL 4.2e-5 (dense position 2050), at most 1.8e-6 at the 42 sparse positions.
